themes.disagreements: High consistency across all model families for both prognosis and interaction, though permutation importance in predictive forests is lower than the strong univariable and causal forest signals.
themes.interpretation: Strong systemic inflammatory marker showing robust evidence for both confounding (outcome prognosis) and effect modification (treatment heterogeneity).
themes.name: Systemic Inflammation

themes.disagreements: Variable signal strength across symptoms; neurological symptoms and nausea show stronger interaction evidence (Causal Forest, R-learner) compared to night sweats and necrotic fluid.
themes.interpretation: Cluster of pretreatment symptomatic indicators exhibiting evidence for both treatment prediction and heterogeneity of effect.
themes.name: Clinical Symptomatology

themes.disagreements: Napsin A expression shows strong interaction evidence, whereas N-stage and NSCLC diagnosis signals are considerably weaker and less consistent across folds.
themes.interpretation: Pathological and staging markers where Napsin A is a credible effect modifier, and N-stage potentially serves as both a confounder and modifier.
themes.name: Disease Pathology and Stage

themes.disagreements: Evidence is primarily driven by predictive forests; univariable signals are weak or absent for MI presence.
themes.interpretation: General health indicators and comorbidities with moderate predictive signals, though myelosuppression exhibits more credible evidence for a dual role.
themes.name: General Health and Comorbidities
